hook_patterns.name: Shocking Industry Threat
hook_patterns.description: Exposes an imminent, highly consequential vulnerability, hack, or corporate catastrophe targeting widely used tech or platforms. The first line startles with scale, while the second names the attacker or impact.
examples: Did you hear that? That's the sound of Microsoft calling up their lawyers on the weekend. Someone
PHP is facing one of its most serious security incidents in years, and if you're running a website built with PHP, WordPress, or Laravel, you need to understand what's happening.

hook_patterns.name: Counterintuitive Fact
hook_patterns.description: Leads with a bizarre or unbelievable truth about a well-known tech figure, company, or hidden feature that contradicts common assumptions.
examples: I bet you had no idea that Justin Bieber changed an entire drug empire in 2014.
Someone is taking a screenshot of your computer every three seconds,
You probably don't know that Estonia keeps a copy of its government data in Luxembourg.

hook_patterns.name: Impossible Feat Claim
hook_patterns.description: Teases a massive, highly technical disruption or reverse-engineering feat accomplished by a lone developer or unexpected actor against industry giants.
examples: How does one gigabyte folder gets compressed to 400 megabyte zip file?
Sony wants you to stop owning your games, so the community rebuilt the PS5 in open source.
This guy just reverse engineered and open sourced every single Adobe product.

hook_patterns.name: Relatable Career Pivot
hook_patterns.description: Starts with an internal monologue or universal anxiety about software engineering, corporate jobs, or salaries to hook professionals instantly.
examples: So I was thinking that I could leave a salary for a job, but I worked in tech.
So you just landed the software engineering job you dreamed about in university.

on_screen_text_style: Bold uppercase kinetic captions highlighting key nouns, tech entities, and verbs. Positioned center-screen with high-contrast text (white text with red/yellow highlights for emphasis) syncing directly with spoken audio to retain viewer attention.
caption_formula: Concise, punchy hook in the first sentence explaining why it matters. Moderate length with 1-2 relevant emojis, followed by 3-5 targeted niche hashtags (#opensource, #tech, #cybersecurity) and a clear CTA.
takeaways: Lead every video by attacking a major tech titan, platform, or exposing an urgent security flaw in the first 3 seconds.
Maintain a brisk pacing of around 3.3 words per second with zero dead air to maximize audience retention.
Use prominent, high-contrast kinetic on-screen text to highlight specific codebases, companies, or tools as they are spoken.
Anchor abstract technical explanations (like reverse engineering or active directory) to tangible real-world consequences.
